newsitem.title: UK: West warns Bosnia strings attached to aid.
newsitem.headline: West warns Bosnia strings attached to aid.

text.p: The West on Thursday warned Bosnian leaders there were strings attached to international aid -- they must stick to the peace agreement hammered out last year or lose the millions of dollars pledged for reconstruction.

"There are important areas of the peace agreement where little progress has been made," the international community said after a two-day conference took stock of the first year of peace after the 43-month war in Bosnia.
Here are the principal points of the agreed action plan:
- For the first time, aid is linked to adherence to Dayton peace agreement. "It isn't going to continue indefinitely," British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind warned.
- The War Crimes Tribunal to be given extra resources
- The International Police Task Force to be boosted in hunt for indicted war criminals
- Greater effort to encourage return of refugees. Of the 2.1 million refugees from the war, only 250,000 have gone home.
- Freedom of Movement task force to ensure Bosnia-wide phone links, common road and rail system, national car number plates and jointly administered airspace.
- Central Bank to be operational by early 1997. Market economy to be set up.
- Media to be allowed to operate free of interference
- End to delay in arms reduction. Mine clearance speeded up.
- Internationally supervised municipal elections to be held by summer of 1997.
- International mediator Carl Bildt to have role strengthened, especially in economic reconstruction.
